rules.cwe_name: Improper Input Validation
rules.description: This reports the external APIs that are used with untrusted data, along with how frequently the API is called, and how many unique sources of untrusted data flow to it.

rules.cwe_name: Function Call With Incorrect Number of Arguments
rules.description: A function is invoked with extra trailing arguments that are ignored.

rules.cwe_name: Use of Potentially Dangerous Function
rules.description: DOM functions that act like 'eval' and execute strings as code are dangerous and impede program analysis and understanding. Consequently, they should not be used.

rules.cwe_name: Assignment to Variable without Use
rules.description: If two functions with the same name are declared in the same scope, one of the declarations overrides the other without warning. This makes the code hard to read and maintain, and may even lead to platform-dependent behavior.

rules.cwe_name: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
rules.description: Deserializing user-controlled data may allow attackers to execute arbitrary code.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
rules.description: Invoking user-controlled methods on certain objects can lead to remote code execution.

rules.cwe_name: Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type ('Type Confusion')
rules.description: Sanitizing an HTTP request parameter may be ineffective if the user controls its type.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
rules.description: Modifying an object obtained via a user-controlled property name may lead to accidental mutation of the built-in Object prototype, and possibly escalate to remote code execution or cross-site scripting.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions
rules.description: Calling a method with a user-controlled name may dispatch to an unexpected target, which could cause an exception.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Argument Delimiters in a Command ('Argument Injection')
rules.description: Forwarding command-line arguments to a child process executed within a shell may indirectly introduce command-line injection vulnerabilities.
